LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
 <security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD follows standard Arch packaging practices for a prebuilt binary package. All sources are pinned with sha256 checksums, and the only external download is the project's own official GitHub releases page (`github.com/duplicati/duplicati/releases/...`). There are no SKIP checksums, no unpinned VCS sources, and no unexpected download hosts. The package installs the provided systemd units, sysusers/tmpfiles configuration, an environment file, and the CLI symlink using standard `install` commands — all within the package's own `/opt/duplicati` and `$pkgdir` scope.

The only moderately notable logic is the `unzip` + `mv "$DEST"/*/* "$DEST"` + `rmdir` sequence used to emulate `--strip-components=1`. This is a well-known idiom for ZIP archives and is not malicious: `rmdir` only removes empty directories, so even if the archive layout were unexpected, it would fail rather than delete data. The `makedepends=(unzip)` is appropriate for this approach. The package makes no network requests during build, contains no obfuscated code, no `eval`/`base64`/`curl|bash`, and does not modify anything outside its own installation paths.

The dependency configuration files (systemd service, sysusers, tmpfiles) are not shown in this excerpt, so their content cannot be audited here — but nothing in this PKGBUILD itself suggests tampering. Overall, this is a clean, well-formed binary package definition with no evidence of supply-chain compromise.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Clean PKGBUILD: checksum-pinned official upstream sources, standard install steps, no malicious behavior found.
</summary>
</security_assessment>
